history.summary: The cheapest psf in the batch ($1,118) for a huge 1163 sqft 2BR at $1.3M, ~6% under the $1,185.5 URA median, with a future CRL Serangoon North station 920m away. Far East/Sino build with decent reviews. But it's 26 years old (~73 yrs lease) — the lease-decay and financing question caps it at Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: Value is the whole thesis: $1,118 psf and a 1163 sqft footprint give the lowest entry-cost-per-sqft here, below the $1,185.5 median, and the 7.6% resale CAGR (131 txns) is well-supported. CRL Serangoon North (CR9, 920m) is a genuine future catalyst and Far East/Sino is a reputable builder with 7.1/10 resident ratings. The counterweight is age — built 2000, ~73 years of lease left and accelerating decay, which weakens financing for future buyers and is the main reason resale liquidity could thin over a 5-7yr hold. Big and cheap, but the lease clock and dated fittings keep it balanced.

history.summary: Very low-quantum $1.39M 3BR (1,152 sqft) at PSF 1206 with 7.6%/yr URA resale appreciation and the future CR9 Serangoon North CRL station as a catalyst. The catch is the lease: 99 years from 1996 means only ~63 years remaining at a 5-7yr exit, which caps financing and the resale buyer pool — a Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: Attractive entry: $1.39M for a 1,152 sqft 3BR keeps the buyer pool wide and the PSF (1206) is roughly at the URA median (1185.5). 7.6%/yr resale CAGR on 131 txns is strong, and CR9 Serangoon North (Cross Island Line, ~2030) is a genuine within-1km catalyst. But the lease commenced 1996 — at a 2032-2033 exit the property is at ~63 years remaining, the zone where CPF usage tightens and the buyer/financing pool narrows, structurally capping appreciation late in the hold. 920m to a not-yet-built MRT and mixed security/maintenance reviews temper enthusiasm. Net: a fairly-priced, cash-flow-decent hold rather than a capital-growth standout.

history.summary: Aging 99-yr (from 1996) Hougang condo where the asking $1,118 psf is essentially at the verified market average (~$1,167 psf), so there is no real bargain — the 'very_low_psf' flag is an age artefact, and a ~73-yr remaining lease that decays over the hold makes this a weak investment.
history.rating_rationale: Web-verified recent Regentville transactions average ~$1,167 psf (range $791-$1,259), so the $1,118 psf ask is roughly at-market, not cheap — consistent with the algo's modest -18.5% age-adj and -6.6% vs-cohort (cohort 21 txns, so reliable). The 'very_low_psf' flag simply reflects that this is a 1999-built, 99-yr-from-1996 development; its low psf is the market correctly pricing an old, decaying lease, not a discount to capture. With ~73 years left and built 1999, lease decay (and approaching the 60-yr financing/CPF-usage thresholds within a 5-7yr hold's resale window) is a structural headwind. No en-bloc (marked 'No') and no dated MRT/zone catalyst. The $1.3M quantum buys a large but dated 2BR with limited forward upside — Avoid for investment.

history.summary: The 06-09 Avoid rested on "ask is at the $1,167 market average" — but that was the size-pooled average (mixing 1,500+ sqft low-psf units). Against the correct same-size cohort (1,151-1,162 sqft, 12-mo median ~$1,198 psf, 9 prints), the $1,118 ask is a genuine ~6-7% discount, so the strongest validated forward signal (cheap-vs-peers in OCR; D19 realized fwd +3.7%/yr) does fire — and the backtest shows cheap old OCR leaseholds outperformed, contradicting the lease-decay narrative. But the cohort band spans $1,066-$1,258 (±9%) including a Mar 2026 print BELOW the ask, so the discount sits inside cohort noise; with <10% of forward variance explainable, this is a near-tie, not an edge — Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: Upgrade from Avoid: the prior at-market claim was a size-pooling error — $1,118 psf is ~6-7% below the same-size 12-mo median (~$1,198, n=9), a real verified discount in the best forward region (OCR), with deep liquidity (580 units, 131 URA txns), low $1.3M quantum, and a dated CR9 Serangoon North catalyst (2030, 920m) inside the 5-7yr hold. Held back from Buy: the discount is modest and within the cohort's ±9% dispersion (Mar 2026 printed $1,066 — below the ask), the CR9 walk is marginal at 11 min, ~69-yr lease (~63 at exit) narrows the late buyer pool, and no en-bloc prospect.
red_flags: Same-size cohort 12-mo band is wide ($1,066-$1,258 psf); Mar 2026 transacted $1,066 — the ask is a premium to the most recent low print
99-yr from 1996 (~69 yrs left, ~63 at exit) — buyer-pool narrowing is gradual but real
CR9 is 920m / 11-min walk — outer edge of MRT benefit; no rail today
No en-bloc prospect (forum chatter only, 2023)
catalysts: CR9 Serangoon North (Cross Island Line) opens 2030 — dated, inside the hold window
Verified ~6-7% discount to same-size 12-mo comps in OCR, the strongest backtested forward signal
Deep liquidity: 580 units, 131 URA txns, ~9 same-size prints/yr; low $1.3M quantum keeps the exit pool broad
5yr resale CAGR 7.6%/yr (no forward power per backtest, but evidences sustained demand)
